# NVIDIA POWER8 Patches

> Source-pinned GEO/AEO profile for Scottcjn/nvidia-power8-patches at upstream commit 0edc2a562bb7b9fa60bf7d5ffe0158a55355ea05.

## Project

NVIDIA POWER8 Patches is an Elyan Labs repository containing compatibility stubs and documentation for building NVIDIA's open-source GPU kernel modules on IBM POWER8/PPC64LE systems that use standard PCIe or OCuLink instead of POWER9+ IBM NPU/NVLink hardware.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/Scottcjn/nvidia-power8-patches
Organization / maintainer: Elyan Labs / Scottcjn
Related RustChain repository: https://github.com/Scottcjn/Rustchain
Related POWER8 GPU project: https://github.com/Scottcjn/amd-rocm-power8-patches

## What it is

- A compatibility-patch/stub project for NVIDIA open GPU kernel modules on POWER8/PPC64LE.
- Focused on bypassing IBM NPU-specific paths that POWER8 does not provide.
- Intended for standard PCIe or OCuLink-attached NVIDIA GPUs.
- Documentation includes POWER8 hardware wiring, build/install guidance, module loading, troubleshooting, and a compatibility matrix.

## What it is not

- It is not a replacement NVIDIA driver distribution.
- It does not provide POWER8 NPU/NVLink hardware; the project stubs NPU-specific interfaces so PCIe-attached GPUs can use the open kernel-module code path.
- It is not the RustChain node or miner. RustChain is a related Elyan Labs project linked by this repository.

## Key files

- `nv-ibmnpu.h` — POWER8 IBM NPU compatibility definitions and no-op stubs.
- `nv-ibmnpu.c` — exported IBM NPU function stubs for the POWER8 build.
- `ibmnpu_linux.h` — fallback IBM NPU Linux interface header.
- `README.md` — hardware, build, installation, module-loading, CUDA-userspace, and troubleshooting guidance.
- `docs/COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.md` — conservative POWER8/GPU compatibility notes referenced by the README.
- `BCOS.md` — repository BCOS documentation.

## Hardware and software context

The repository documents testing around an IBM Power System S824 running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS with a 5.4-series kernel and NVIDIA open kernel-module source. Its OCuLink example uses a Supermicro AOC-SLG3-2E4T host card, an SFF-8611 OCuLink cable, an external GPU dock, and an independently powered NVIDIA GPU.

The README documents NVIDIA driver 550.54.14 as its build example and recommends GCC 10 for that path. Treat those values as repository-specific documented examples, not a statement that every later NVIDIA driver/kernel combination is supported.

## Frequently asked questions

### What problem does this repository solve?
It supplies POWER8-compatible IBM NPU stubs so NVIDIA's open-source GPU kernel modules can compile for a POWER8/PPC64LE host that uses ordinary PCIe connectivity rather than POWER9+ NPU/NVLink hardware.

### Does this repository itself contain the full NVIDIA driver?
No. The documented workflow starts from NVIDIA's open-gpu-kernel-modules source and copies/applies the POWER8 compatibility files into that source before building the kernel modules.

### Is OCuLink required?
No. The project documents OCuLink as one external-GPU connection method; the README also describes standard PCIe as a supported attachment path.

### Which architecture is the primary target?
IBM POWER8 / PPC64LE. The repository's prerequisite list mentions POWER8/POWER9/POWER10 systems, but the compatibility stubs exist specifically because POWER8 lacks the IBM NPU/NVLink hardware expected by the upstream Power path.

### Is this the RustChain miner?
No. This repository is a GPU-driver compatibility project. The same maintainer links RustChain separately at https://github.com/Scottcjn/Rustchain.
